title: MS-101: Independent Scientific Validation, Identifiability and Uncertainty
body:
## Objective
Establish what the motion-matching product can claim scientifically, separately from engines agreeing with each other.

## Scope and Deliverables
- Move the identifiability assessment from MS-90 to the beginning of model calibration. Audit the tour-average capture's provenance, compositing, temporal registration, segment rigidity, external-force availability and physically feasible interpretation. Do not assume averaged marker motion represents a realizable individual trial.
- Predeclare calibration versus held-out validation datasets, supported subject/club/motion domain, marker protocols and known limitations. Require multiple independent subjects/trials representative of the release domain; fix the validation cohort and thresholds before tuning, with a biomechanical reviewer-approved rationale for sample coverage. Driver and iron examples alone are not generalization evidence.
- Assess parameter and state identifiability (scaled Jacobian singular values/null directions per phase, synthetic recovery, sensitivity to marker noise/gaps/offsets, anthropometry, filtering and contact assumptions). Report uncertainty for outputs; do not call an unidentifiable contact optimum a measured parameter.
- Validate forces/loads against synchronized measured ground-reaction forces, center of pressure and independent outputs where those claims are offered. Validate muscle-related claims with appropriate independent evidence; fitting kinematics alone is insufficient. Missing experimental data blocks the affected claim and remains an explicit acquisition task with owner, dataset requirements and provenance/usage rights.
- Reuse design-manual calculation governance and industrial-readiness registry. Produce a validation protocol, held-out results, reviewer decision and explicit supported/unsupported claims; no new approval registry.

## Acceptance Tests
Held-out results are generated without parameter retuning or capture-specific code edits; uncertainty coverage and domain failures are reported. Synthetic unobservable parameters are detected. Physiologically unsupported outputs cannot be labeled validated in UI/export. Review rationale links evidence to every shipped scientific claim.

## Dependencies and Ownership
Protocol/data audit starts immediately with MS-90 phase A; consumes MS-100 metric definitions. Final results consume MS-104 qualified fits and MS-108 observable golf metrics. Accountable role: scientific/biomechanics lead with independent reviewer; coordinator owns missing-data acquisition plan. Blocks professional release scientific claims.

## Execution and Evidence Contract
Part of epic #10363; owner-authorized contract revision 2026-09-17. This issue is planning, not evidence of implementation or qualification.
Before implementation, check/post the existing issue lease and register presence through Repository_Management; preserve existing owners and worktrees. Use the established source modules, candidate/receipt schemas, feature-parity and industrial-readiness registries. No parallel metrics or acceptance authority.
Use focused topic PRs with issue references, repo-standard validation, relevant native-engine tests, and negative-path tests. Mocks or skipped native tests cannot qualify a native engine. Update the canonical handoff and the existing governing-issue development-log row in place. Store content-addressed evidence with source/model/data/runtime/contract hashes; keep historical evidence immutable and mark superseded verdicts explicitly. Workflow changes follow the Repository_Management fleet campaign process.
The program coordinator allocates a lease holder before implementation; the accountable role below is not a claim that an agent has accepted the task. Release remains blocked until the linked evidence passes the revised contracts.

## Program Qualification Dependencies
- MS-100 (#10374): Fail-Closed Metrics and Versioned Physical Acceptance Qualification
- MS-104 (#10378): Full-Swing Qualification for All Six Engines and Flagship Models
- MS-108 (#10382): Observable Golf Outputs, Impact Semantics and Accuracy Budgets
